scenes.title: Cold open
narration: Performers wield tennis-ball sized poi on cords—modern ones fashioned from plastic shopping bags—while singing in European-style harmony.
This is Kapa haka. 19th century origin, modern festival.
on_screen: Title card: Kapa haka · New Zealand (Aotearoa) · 19th century origin, modern festival

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Modern kapa haka stems from pre-European Māori performing arts including haka, weapon training, poi, and mōteatea.
Concert groups emerged in the 1860s, particularly in Rotorua, to perform for tourists by blending European and Māori musical principles.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Kapa haka serves as a vital vehicle for expressing cultural Polynesian identity, preserving genealogy, and celebrating community heritage.
It features prominently at biennial national competitions like Te Matatini and school festivals.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Performers stand in synchronized rows, mixing foot stamping, body percussion, and hand gestures.
Women execute graceful poi swings and the wiri hand tremor, while men lead front-row haka challenges with aggressive facial expressions and body postures.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Music is primarily vocal, featuring European-style choral harmony accompanied by acoustic guitars.
The only physical instruments and sound-makers utilized are guitars, pūtatara conch shells, the percussive striking of poi, rākau sticks, and foot stamping.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Groups wear traditional or neo-Māori attire.
Performances take place on stage during festivals, community gatherings, and competitions, lasting up to 40 minutes per complete suite.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Performances are led by kaitataki (male and female leaders) who move among the group to urge them on.
Composers, arrangers, choreographers, and costume designers also drive the art form.
Groups form through extended family, iwi (tribe), school, or regional associations across New Zealand, presenting varied regional compositions and performance styles at national events.
Directly descended from ancestral Māori performing arts, incorporating pre-colonial weaponry, chant, and warrior training methods into modern choral and competitive suites.

music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Kapa haka (New Zealand (Aotearoa)). New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
